title: drain-shadowing-caused-routing-amplification-and-fallback-surge-postmortem
creator: Maya Patel
description: Postmortem for a production incident where a combination of stale drain metadata and an out-of-order capacity update caused a large fraction of traffic to be misrouted into a lower-tier variant, triggering cascading fallbacks and a token-cost/latency spike. This ticket captures timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and recommended long-term fixes.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~22:47 UTC a regional drain sequence entered a partial state where the control plane had marked nodes draining but the routing layer continued to receive stale capacity hints. A subset of in-flight requests were redirected away from the intended regional pool to a cheaper variant (quantized v2) without warm caches; when those requests failed to meet latency SLOs they triggered automatic fallback to the highest-throughput variant in the fallback policy, amplifying load and causing a cascade of fallbacks across tiers. The cascade lasted ~16 minutes before manual mitigation stabilized routing. Impact: 11% p99 latency increase for affected customers, a 4.2x increase in per-token egress for the cascade window, and 23 customer support tickets for degraded responses.
timeline: 2026-03-09 22:42 UTC: Regional capacity rebalancer initiated a drain for us-east-2 pool to do kernel upgrades.
2026-03-09 22:46 UTC: Control plane wrote drain intent; worker agents acknowledged but one scheduling heartbeat was lost during a transient network blip.
2026-03-09 22:47:30 UTC: Routing cache refresh read a mix of old and new capacity hints leading to partial shadow drain state for ~12% of routes.
2026-03-09 22:48:10 UTC: Traffic routed to quantized v2 variant (fallback policy allowed variant swap). Kv-cache misses and cold kernels increased token latency and error rate on that variant.

2026-03-09 22:49:00 UTC: Automatic fallback policy triggered, routing a bulk of the failing requests to the high-throughput variant. This caused saturation on GPU pools serving that variant and injected extra cross-region traffic.
2026-03-09 23:03 UTC: On-call engineering observed alert: region-fallback-rate > threshold and p99 latency spike; mitigations started.
2026-03-09 23:07 UTC: Manual routing override applied to pin critical customer routes to their original regional pool; auto-fallback disabled while we repaired drain metadata.
2026-03-09 23:12 UTC: Drain tombstone reconciliation completed; routing caches invalidated and warmed variant pools rebalanced.
2026-03-09 23:18 UTC: System returned to normal routing; post-incident monitoring kept elevated watch for 2 hours.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Postmortem investigation kickoff; cross-team retrospective scheduled.
2026-03-12 15:00 UTC: Root cause confirmed after replaying controller events and routing cache snapshots.
root_cause: A race between control-plane drain intent publication and routing cache refresh combined with insufficiently conservative fallback policies. Specifically: (1) drain intent was partially applied due to a lost worker heartbeat leaving some nodes advertising capacity while internal state flagged them draining (drain-shadowing); (2) the routing layer accepted the stale capacity hints and selected a variant allowed by the fallback policy even though that variant had cold caches and different performance characteristics; (3) the aggressive fallback-on-error policy immediately promoted a higher-throughput variant, creating a demand surge and resource contention. Lack of atomic drain state transitions and weak invariants between the control plane and routing cache allowed inconsistent decisions.
immediate_actions: Applied manual routing override to pin critical routes to healthy regional pools (rollback flag enabled).
Paused automatic fallback triggers for the affected tenants to stop cascading variant swaps.
Invalidated routing cache entries for the region and forced a full refresh with strong consistency checks.
Scaled up warm pools for the quantized and high-throughput variants to reduce cold-start penalty while rebalancing.
Notified SRE, runtime, and product teams; posted customer status updates and opened a targeted support triage channel.
long_term_fixes: Introduce atomic drain state machine: publish drain intent + apply tombstone marker only after worker heartbeat confirmation; routing layer must treat partial drains as 'do not route' until tombstone is authoritative (ENG-21610).
Add a TTL + tombstone propagation mechanism: stale capacity hints must expire and be ignored if not refreshed by authoritative control-plane snapshot (ENG-21611).

Harden fallback policy defaults: require at-least-one-successful-call or warmed-cache signal before promoting to a new variant; add exponential backoff and circuit-breaker on cross-variant promotions (ENG-21612).
Extend routing observability: new metrics for 'drain-shadowed routes', 'fallback-amplification-factor', and per-variant cold-start error rate; add a dashboard and automated alarms (ENG-21613).
Control-plane/routing integration tests: simulate partial drain states and network partitions in the integration test harness to catch state drift before release (ENG-21614).
Add canary for fallback-behavior changes: enable conservative fallback only for low-risk tenants initially and monitor at the release-level (release: runtime-1.23).
follow_up_tasks: ENG-21610 - implement atomic drain state machine in control plane and workers
ENG-21611 - TTL + tombstone propagation and routing cache expiry
ENG-21612 - fallback policy conservative mode + circuit-breakers
ENG-21613 - observability: dashboards and alerts for drain-shadow and amplification
ENG-21614 - integration tests for drain/routing partitions
ENG-21705 - update runbooks and on-call playbooks to include 'drain-shadow' detection and manual rollback steps
notes: Key learning: aggressive, opaque automation (autoscaling + automatic variant promotion) needs stronger invariants and observability. We've prioritized conservative defaults that trade a small amount of available throughput for predictability and cost control. The proposed fixes will be split across two sprints with a small canary rollout in runtime-1.23.
conclusion: Incident resolved; root cause identified and path to remediation agreed. Action items scheduled and prioritized. We reduced blast radius by making fallback behavior less permissive and improving drain-state correctness to avoid similar cascades in future.
